nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior.label: Own-rating margin and total prior for the game-state distribution (market-free)
nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior.measurement: Expected margin = (off_epa_A - def_epa_B) - (off_epa_B - def_epa_A) per play x expected plays per team (nfl.pace), plus a home-field constant fitted on 2015-2025 games (about 1.5 points, refit yearly) and a starter-QB adjustment from nfl.qb_efficiency versus the replacement backup; EPA inputs use a 10-game exponential half-life (about 6 games) shrunk to league mean with k=6 games, opponent-adjusted by ridge. Expected total = sum of the two team expected plays x points per play. Margin sd = 13.0 points, total sd = 9.5 points, re-estimated from own residuals. As-of: last game before kickoff, QB and injury status at the latest inactive list. Contains no spread_line, total_line or moneyline.
nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior.mechanism: Builds the distribution of the expected score path from the team's own offence and defence ratings, home edge and starter quarterback status, so nfl.script is fed without any sportsbook spread or total.
nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior.rationale: nfl.script's catalog measurement integrates over a margin distribution centred on the point spread; that makes the volume driver an echo of the market. The margin and total centre must come from own opponent-adjusted EPA ratings so it can be compared against Kalshi prices rather than copied from them.

nfl.own_team_rating_market_free.label: Own opponent-adjusted team rating with preseason prior (market-free)
nfl.own_team_rating_market_free.measurement: Weekly update: rating_t in points of margin per game from ridge regression of capped game margin (cap 24) on team and opponent indicators, home indicator (home-field constant fitted yearly, about 1.5 points) over all games since the prior season, weights exp(-ln2 x games_ago/10); combine 50/50 with an opponent-adjusted EPA/play margin rating converted to points (points margin per game = EPA/play margin x about 63 plays per team per game, a conversion to be refit yearly). Preseason prior = 0.67 x last season's final rating (one third reversion to zero) + 0.10 points x (returning-production percent above league mean)/10 + starting-QB change adjustment (QB value difference per nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop) with prior sd 4.0 points (assumption to be recalibrated against 2002-2025 final ratings). Posterior sd after n games = 1/sqrt(1/4.0^2 + n/13.5^2) points (13.5 is a standard deviation, so n/182.25). As-of: kickoff of the next game; no spread, total or moneyline enters.
nfl.own_team_rating_market_free.mechanism: A Bayesian margin rating per team built only from game results, play-level EPA, roster continuity and quarterback status, with a home-field constant and a preseason prior, used as the latent strength for every futures simulation.
nfl.own_team_rating_market_free.rationale: Every contract in this archetype depends on team strength, and nfl.ratings is built by inverting spreads and totals, which makes it a copy of the market. A rating from results, EPA and roster inputs can be compared with Kalshi prices as an independent estimate; the subtle part is the preseason prior, which dominates in September and October.

nfl.paired_score_covariance_own.label: Paired team-score covariance from pace, script and weather (market-free)
nfl.paired_score_covariance_own.measurement: Using 2010-2025 games compute the residual correlation of the two team scores after subtracting each team's own model mean, in bins of the expected total (own model total from the two means: low <40, mid 40-50, high >50 points), expected plays (nfl.pace) and wind (calm <10 mph, windy >=15 mph); shrink bin correlations toward the pooled value with k=150 games; sample score pairs from a Gaussian copula with the bin correlation over the two nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean marginals; add a home-field and venue shift (nfl.venue, home team mean +1.5 points, dome flag) into each mean. Output: P(both >= 35) and the correlation by bin. As-of: kickoff forecasts.
nfl.paired_score_covariance_own.mechanism: Estimates the covariance between the two teams' scores through shared pace, shared weather and the zero-sum score path, so the joint tail for the both-teams-35 contract is not a product of marginals.
nfl.paired_score_covariance_own.rationale: Team scores are positively correlated through plays and drives and conditionally negative through script (a leading team slows play and shortens the other side's comeback window). The joint tail P(both >= 35) is a tail of a score pair and is highly sensitive to the correlation sign at high totals.

nfl.pass_run_split_epa_both_sides.label: Pass and run EPA split for both offence and defence, opponent-adjusted
nfl.pass_run_split_epa_both_sides.measurement: For each team compute offensive EPA per dropback and EPA per rush and defensive EPA per dropback faced and per rush faced from 2016-present play-by-play (excluding kneel-downs, spikes and garbage time at win probability above 95 percent), opponent-adjusted by a ridge regression over the last 12 games with exponential half-life 6 games; shrink each component toward the league mean with k=150 plays for pass and k=100 plays for rush. Expected points rate = pass share x (off pass EPA - opponent pass defence EPA) + run share x (off rush EPA - opponent run defence EPA), with pass share from nfl.pace-adjusted neutral pass rate. As-of last completed game.
nfl.pass_run_split_epa_both_sides.mechanism: Separates each side's points production and prevention into pass and rush components so the matchup between an offence's style and the defence's pass and run strengths can be computed.
nfl.pass_run_split_epa_both_sides.rationale: Collapsing the opposing defence to one defensive EPA hides whether it is strong against the pass or the run; a pass-heavy offence is hurt by a pass-defence strength and a run-heavy one by a run-defence strength. The split needs both offences and both defences with enough shrinkage.

nfl.per_game_rate_persistence.label: Within-season persistence of per-game rate (variance components)
nfl.per_game_rate_persistence.measurement: For each statistic and position fit a mixed model on 2012-2025 player-games: y_game = u_player-season + e_game, with u from a normal distribution and e from a count distribution; estimate the ratio sigma_u / sigma_e and the ICC by position and stat; apply to project season total variance = n x Var(e) + n^2 x Var(u) over remaining games; use the current-season estimate of u as the posterior mean with shrinkage proportional to games played.
nfl.per_game_rate_persistence.mechanism: Decomposition of per-game output variance into a persistent player-season component and a game-level noise component.
nfl.per_game_rate_persistence.rationale: Season-sum variance is sqrt(n) times game sd only if games are independent; role persistence makes the sum more dispersed, so the probability of reaching distant rungs is larger than an independent model says.

nfl.period_drive_scoring_rates.label: Opponent-adjusted per-drive TD/FG rates by period
nfl.period_drive_scoring_rates.measurement: Multinomial (TD, FG, no score) logistic with team offence and opponent defence random effects per period, fitted on 3 seasons with exponential decay (half-life 12 team games); shrink period effects to the team's all-period rate with k=30 drives; as-of previous game; exclude garbage-time Q4 drives (win probability <5% or >95%) from the training sample and treat them separately.
nfl.period_drive_scoring_rates.mechanism: Per-drive probability of TD, FG and no score separately for Q1, Q2 (including two-minute drives), Q3 and Q4 by team and opponent.
nfl.period_drive_scoring_rates.rationale: Team quality is measured on all plays; period rates differ because scripted openers and hurry-up drills have different efficiency, and Q4 depends on game state; averaging understates the spread of per-quarter rates.

nfl.period_zero_tie_mass.mechanism: Empirical and model probabilities of 0-0 in a quarter, an equal non-zero score, and BTTS by quarter.

nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit.label: Extreme-value tail fit for play length (long plays and long kicks)
nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit.measurement: Using all regular-season plays since 1999, fit a peaks-over-threshold model (threshold 60 yards for plays, 56 yards for kick distance) with Poisson exceedance rate per 1,000 snaps by start-yardline bucket and an era term (pre-2024, 2024, 2025+ kicking rules) on the kick tail; fit offensive gains and turnover-return lengths separately so either contract reading can be priced; propagate parameter uncertainty by posterior or bootstrap; output P(max >= 99) and P(max kick >= 70) for N remaining games with the running maximum to date as the as-of state.
nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit.mechanism: Generalized Pareto or Gumbel-type fit to the upper tail of scrimmage-play and kick lengths, giving return levels for the league-wide season maximum.
nfl.play_length_evt_tail_fit.rationale: The contract is a threshold on a maximum, so only the extreme tail matters. A bulk model (mean yards per play) is nearly irrelevant, and the cap of 99 yards plus the finite number of own-goal-line snaps means a bounded-tail fit with exposure weighting is required. Few historical points mean parameter uncertainty must be carried into the probability.

nfl.player_destination_choice.label: Next-team categorical choice for a named player (incl. current team and retire/no team)
nfl.player_destination_choice.measurement: Two-stage: P(move) from contract status (under contract years, tag eligibility, age, retirement signals) by logistic regression on 2012-2025 veteran offseasons; conditional on move, multinomial logit over 31 teams with features = projected cap space at the window, positional starter quality gap (team's current starter value vs player), draft capital, head-coach/scheme ties, reported-interest flag; P(retire/no team) from age and position base rates; as-of market time; shrink team utilities toward uniform with a Dirichlet prior (alpha=1).
nfl.player_destination_choice.mechanism: Distribution over the player's team on a date: remain with current team, each other team, or retire/unsigned, from contract status, team cap space and positional need.
nfl.player_destination_choice.rationale: Next-team markets list every candidate team plus the current team and a residual; the current team often carries most mass (contract, tag, extension), and other teams are ranked by cap space, need and reported interest, not by quality alone.

nfl.player_longest_reception_max_model.label: Player single-game longest reception model (max of K catches vs strike)
nfl.player_longest_reception_max_model.measurement: K ~ negative binomial: targets forecast (nfl.targets) times catch probability (nfl.catch_rate_oe), dispersion fit on last 2 seasons; per-catch length = air yards (nfl.air_yards_adot, depth mixture) plus YAC, from the player's last 24 games with half-life 8 games, shrunk to position-role with 60 catches prior, adjusted by coverage matchup; compute 1 - sum_k P(K=k) F(s)^k at each strike; multiply by 1 - P(no live snap | active).
nfl.player_longest_reception_max_model.mechanism: P(longest reception > strike | plays) = 1 - E[F(strike)^K], where K is the number of receptions and F the player's per-catch length CDF in this matchup.
nfl.player_longest_reception_max_model.rationale: The contract ignores total yards: one long catch settles YES and zero catches settles NO, so volume enters through K and the upper tail of per-catch length matters more than the mean. Active-no-play settles at the fair price, so the forecastable part is conditional on a live snap.

nfl.player_reception_length_distribution.label: Player reception-length distribution (air yards plus yards after catch), incl. longest-play probability
nfl.player_reception_length_distribution.measurement: For each receiver, take receptions from the last 24 games (min 40; pooled to position-alignment template with k=30 receptions otherwise), fit a log-normal/ Pareto splice at the 85th percentile; then P(longest >= x | N catches) = 1 - F(x)^N with N drawn from the projected receptions distribution. Opponent factor = opposing defence's allowed explosive-reception rate vs league (k=120). Units: probabilities for each strike.
nfl.player_reception_length_distribution.mechanism: Empirical distribution of this receiver's yards per reception and probability that any single reception exceeds 20, 30, 40 and 60 yards.
nfl.player_reception_length_distribution.rationale: The longest-reception market and the escalator tails need the upper tail of catch lengths, which differs from the mean yards per catch; YAC-heavy slot players and deep WRs have the same mean and very different tails.

nfl.player_single_game_yardage_extreme_r.label: Player-game probability of a 200/225/250+ single-game rushing total
nfl.player_single_game_yardage_extreme_r.measurement: For each rusher-game simulate carries ~ negative binomial (mean from nfl.carries share times team rush attempts conditioned on the market-free expected margin from nfl.own_team_rating_market_free, no spread) and per-carry yards from the rusher's discrete tail (nfl.rush_yardage_tail) adjusted by opponent explosive-allowed rate; P(sum >= 225). Calibrate on 2000-2025 200+ yard games (frequency per season); apply a starter-pull cap at margins above 28 in the fourth quarter. As-of start of week.
nfl.player_single_game_yardage_extreme_r.mechanism: Per player-game probability that rushing yards reach a high rung (200, 225, 250) from the compound of carry count and heavy-tailed per-carry yards, conditioned on script and opponent.
nfl.player_single_game_yardage_extreme_r.rationale: Mean-based projections put no back near 225 yards; the event, which recurs across seasons (record 296 yards), comes from a lead back getting 30 carries in a lopsided win against a poor run defence and breaking two long runs. The compound distribution, not the mean, decides, and quarterbacks with designed runs are a second, smaller contributor.

nfl.player_trade_hazard.label: Named-player trade hazard before a date
nfl.player_trade_hazard.measurement: Discrete-time weekly logistic hazard trained on 2010-2025 player-weeks: covariates = team win% minus preseason model expectation, weeks to trade deadline (indicator of final 2 weeks), dead cap if traded / cap hit, years of control remaining, age, positional value tier, credible-report flag (from nfl.insider_report_conversion); P(trade before date) = 1 - prod(1 - h_w) over weeks to the date; base-rate shrinkage toward position-season frequency with k=500 player-seasons; as-of each week.
nfl.player_trade_hazard.mechanism: Probability that a named player is traded (officially processed) within a window, from team contention status, contract structure and reported availability.
nfl.player_trade_hazard.rationale: Trades cluster before the trade deadline and in the offseason; most players have near-zero hazard, so team context and contract terms (dead cap, years of control) separate candidates, and reports of shopping are the strongest signal.

nfl.player_xtd.label: Player expected touchdowns (xTD) from play-level opportunity
nfl.player_xtd.measurement: For each rush attempt or target in the player's last 17 team games (half-life 6 games), assign P(TD | yardline_100, down, ydstogo, play_type, is_target) from a league-wide model fit on 2006+ pbp; sum by player; divide by team xTD to get a share. Shrink share to positional prior with k=4 team games' worth of goal-line touches. As-of: through the previous game; recompute after inactives.
nfl.player_xtd.mechanism: Each rushing attempt and target carries a modelled TD probability that depends on yard line, down and distance, and play type; summing gives an opportunity-based TD expectation independent of luck.
nfl.player_xtd.rationale: Season TD counts and TD rates are dominated by finishing luck (a back with 6 carries inside the 5 can score 0-6). xTD collapses to the opportunity and removes the single-season noise that makes nfl.td_rates misleading.

nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model.label: Prospect slot dispersion model (consensus rank to realized pick distribution)
nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model.measurement: From 2010-2026 drafts (all seven rounds), join point-in-time consensus rank (mean of public boards dated 90, 30 and 1 days before the draft, excluding mocks and boards that cite sportsbook odds) to realized pick; fit a quantile or ordinal regression of pick on rank, position and days-to-draft with a QB and EDGE premium and spread rising with rank, and an undrafted mass beyond the board; produce a slot pmf per prospect and a cross-prospect order-statistic simulation. Shrink thin positions toward the pooled model with 20 draftees of prior weight.
nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model.mechanism: Empirical distribution of realized pick minus consensus rank by rank band and position, giving heavy-tailed, skewed slot distributions that vary by position premium.
nfl.prospect_slot_dispersion_model.rationale: Consensus boards give a central ranking, but markets ask for ordinal events (1st overall, top 5, before pick N, 3rd quarterback). The spread of realized slot around consensus grows with rank, is asymmetric for quarterbacks (they are taken early) and depends on how close the point-in-time board was to the draft.

nfl.qb_attempt_forecast.mechanism: Forecast distribution of the QB's attempts using team plays, pass rate conditional on expected state, sacks, wind and QB participation.
nfl.qb_attempt_forecast.rationale: Attempts are the exposure for TDs, completions and INTs; ignoring their conditional distribution across scripts mixes games where the QB throws 25 times and 45 times.

nfl.qb_blowout_pull_hazard.label: QB blowout pull and early-exit hazard

nfl.qb_blowout_pull_hazard.mechanism: Probability that the QB leaves the game early because of a lopsided score or injury, as a function of lead and time.
nfl.qb_blowout_pull_hazard.rationale: Protected and standard contracts differ on pulls; a QB pulled up 28 in the fourth quarter has truncated counts and the protected contract voids.

nfl.qb_blowout_pull_threshold.label: Quarterback benching rule: margin and clock at which the starter is pulled
nfl.qb_blowout_pull_threshold.measurement: For each head coach, over the last 3 seasons (min 8 qualifying games, shrink toward league mean with k=6 games), record the lead (points) and game-clock minute at which the starter QB's last snap occurred in games decided by 17+; fit a logistic: P(starter pulled | lead, minutes_remaining). Output pre-game: P(pull before Q4 ends) = integral over simulated margin paths, as-of the last pre-game depth chart. Unit: probability and expected minutes lost.
nfl.qb_blowout_pull_threshold.mechanism: Head-coach-specific rule for resting the starter in lopsided games, which removes dropbacks on the winning side and sets the zero-attempt atom after halftime for the protected variant.
nfl.qb_blowout_pull_threshold.rationale: Existing exit-risk input treats injury and benching together. For a quarterback on a heavy favourite, benching is a coach habit tied to margin and minutes remaining, not a physical hazard; it lowers the top rungs even when the pre-game model expects a high-yardage game and decides whether a protected contract refunds.

nfl.qb_career_milestone_accrual.label: Season and career passing-TD accrual model with games and aging
nfl.qb_career_milestone_accrual.measurement: Per-game TD mean from nfl.qb_expected_pass_td and attempt forecast, trend by age (QB aging curve estimated 2000-2025: attempts flat then decline from age 35, TD rate regressed), games remaining from schedule minus byes, availability from injury hazard (QB games missed per season by age and mobility, beta prior); simulate season totals with negative binomial game counts; as-of previous game.
nfl.qb_career_milestone_accrual.mechanism: Projected remaining TDs given per-game rate, games remaining, availability and aging curve.
nfl.qb_career_milestone_accrual.rationale: Season (40+) and career markets are sums over games; the distribution of games played and a QB's age-related change in TD rate matter as much as the per-game mean.

nfl.qb_challenger_prior.label: Incumbent-versus-challenger quarterback value gap (draft-capital prior for unproven QBs)
nfl.qb_challenger_prior.measurement: gap_w = EPA_incumbent_w - EPA_challenger_prior_w where EPA_incumbent_w is the incumbent's opponent-adjusted EPA per dropback over the last 8 games with a prior of league-average QB EPA at weight 150 dropbacks, and EPA_challenger_prior_w = a regression of first-3-season EPA per dropback on log draft pick (2000-2025 QBs with at least 150 dropbacks) blended with the challenger's own preseason and in-game dropbacks using weight n/(n+150). Pick number enters as a continuous slope, undrafted as pick 260. Output the gap and its SD for the discrete-time logistic hazard in nfl.qb_change_hazard. As-of: after each game, with bye weeks excluded from the exposure count.
nfl.qb_challenger_prior.mechanism: The expected performance gap between the incumbent starter and a challenger drives benching and promotion decisions; for rookies and players with few dropbacks the challenger's value rests on a prior built from draft position.
nfl.qb_challenger_prior.rationale: The first-start contracts (KXNFLFIRSTSTART, KXNFLDEBUT) are about a named unproven QB overtaking an incumbent, and the incumbent's in-season EPA alone ignores how good the challenger is expected to be; teams that spent a high pick tolerate a shorter leash for the incumbent.

nfl.qb_change_hazard.label: Starting-QB change hazard (benching or promotion) by week
nfl.qb_change_hazard.measurement: Discrete-time logistic hazard on QB-weeks 2010-2025: incumbent EPA+CPOE composite vs prior, team record, turnovers, week since bye, challenger draft round and contract, coach tenure, owner pressure; shrink coefficients with ridge; output weekly h and cumulative probability over contract window excluding byes; as-of report date.
nfl.qb_change_hazard.mechanism: Per-week hazard that the depth chart lists a different starting QB than the previous week.
nfl.qb_change_hazard.rationale: First-start contracts are about the hazard of leaving the starter's role; incumbent performance, team record and the next QB's draft capital govern it, and the weeks right after the bye are higher hazard.
raw_data: QB-week table: starter id, performance, record, depth chart, bye

nfl.qb_completion_count_model.label: QB completion-count model: expected completion probability by attempt mix with accuracy over expected (market-free)
nfl.qb_completion_count_model.measurement: Per QB-offence: xComp per attempt = mean nflfastR cp (completion probability) over the last 16 games with half-life 8 games; completion over expected = mean cpoe shrunk toward 0 with k=300 attempts; opponent factor = opponent's allowed (complete_pass - cp) over the last 12 games, shrunk with k=250 attempts; p = xComp + cpoe_shrunk + opp_factor (all on the probability scale, clipped to [0.35, 0.85]) with a wind >15 mph adjustment of -2 percentage points. Completions | attempts ~ beta-binomial(attempts, p, rho), rho estimated from 2018-2025 QB-games (about 0.01-0.02). Mixed over the nfl.qb_attempt_forecast distribution. As-of: end of the previous game.
nfl.qb_completion_count_model.mechanism: Converts a forecast attempt distribution into a completions distribution using per-attempt expected completion probability (target depth, pressure, receiver separation) plus the QB's shrunk completion-over-expected.
nfl.qb_completion_count_model.rationale: Completion rungs settle on a thinned count; raw completion percentage confounds the QB's accuracy with his offence's target-depth mix and the opponent's coverage, and is noisy over a few games. Separating expected completion probability (scheme and matchup) from completion over expected (QB skill, heavily regressed) is what moves a 25+ completions rung when attempts are fixed.

nfl.qb_dropback_to_attempt_leakage.label: Dropback-to-attempt leakage rate (sack, scramble, spike, kneel) for the QB-offence pair
nfl.qb_dropback_to_attempt_leakage.measurement: Per QB over his last 17 starts, time-decayed with half-life 8 games: (sacks + scrambles + spikes) / dropbacks, shrunk toward the offence-level rate with k=150 dropbacks. Pre-game forecast = QB rate adjusted by opponent pressure rate allowed relative to league (log-odds additive), capped to 3 sd. Units: fraction of dropbacks.
nfl.qb_dropback_to_attempt_leakage.mechanism: Share of dropbacks that never become passing attempts because they end in sacks, scrambles or clock-stopping spikes.
nfl.qb_dropback_to_attempt_leakage.rationale: Passing yards credit only attempts and official QB yardage is gross, so the attempts count is dropbacks times (1 - leakage). Leakage is the interaction of the opponent pressure rate and this passer's tendency to escape or hold the ball; two quarterbacks with equal EPA per dropback can differ by 4-6 attempts per game from this alone.

nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop.label: Team-specific quarterback scenario tree and rating drop to the backup
nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop.measurement: For each team, rating drop = (QB1 value - QB2 value) in points, where QB value = career-regressed EPA per dropback prior x dropbacks x conversion (about 0.2 points of margin per 0.01 EPA per dropback per game, from regression), shrunk to league mean with k=300 dropbacks; missed-game distribution from historical QB games missed by age and injury history (negative binomial); scenario tree: QB1 all games, partial, absent. nfl.qb_scenario_rating_drop.rationale: Quarterback change is the largest swing in team rating, and the size of the drop varies from one point for teams with a competent backup to ten points for teams with a replacement-level one.

nfl.qb_scramble_yield_given_pressure.label: Quarterback scramble and designed-run yield conditioned on pressure
nfl.qb_scramble_yield_given_pressure.measurement: For each QB, scrambles per pressured dropback and yards per scramble over the last 24 games (half-life 12), designed-run carries per game from the last 12; shrink with k=80 dropbacks (scramble) and k=5 games (designed). Opponent adjustment: opposing pressure rate (log-odds) and spy/contain tendencies from charting. Output: expected carries and yards with variance. Needs pressure flags from a charting vendor or the sack/hit proxy.
nfl.qb_scramble_yield_given_pressure.mechanism: For a quarterback: probability that a pressured dropback becomes a scramble, yards per scramble and designed-run carries per game by situation.
nfl.qb_scramble_yield_given_pressure.rationale: For quarterback rushing contracts yardage arises from scrambles under pressure and from scheme, not from handoffs; scramble conversion depends on coverage downfield and on the passer's mobility, and designed runs are a coaching feature.

nfl.qb_target_concentration.label: Quarterback target concentration and first-read lean
nfl.qb_target_concentration.measurement: For each quarterback, compute target-share Herfindahl over his last 20 starts (half-life 10 games, min 200 targets; shrink to team-level with k=150 targets) and the primary receiver's share. Apply to the receiver under study as a multiplier on expected target share relative to neutral dispersion: share_adj = share x (1 + b x (conc - league_conc)) with b estimated by out-of-sample regression.
nfl.qb_target_concentration.mechanism: Gini or Herfindahl of the quarterback's targets across his receivers, plus the share to the primary read in the last 20 starts.
nfl.qb_target_concentration.rationale: A quarterback who locks onto one receiver gives that receiver both a higher mean and a higher variance, and when the primary receiver is out the concentration determines how widely targets spread.

nfl.quarter_total_order_statistics.label: Joint four-quarter total distribution: argmax quarter (with dead-heat share) and P(minimum quarter = 0)
nfl.quarter_total_order_statistics.measurement: Run >=20,000 drive-level simulations per game using period drive counts (nfl.drive_clock_allocation), period per-drive TD/FG/safety rates (nfl.period_drive_scoring_rates) and the halftime-state mixture for Q3/Q4; for each draw compute T_q (combined points, regulation only, OT excluded), payout_q = 1{T_q = max}/#{argmax}, and 1{min_q T_q = 0}; average. Calibrate against 2012-2025 empirical frequencies by expected-total decile (isotonic on P(min=0) and on Q2/Q4 argmax shares). As-of: inputs frozen at the Friday injury report plus kickoff weather forecast.
nfl.quarter_total_order_statistics.mechanism: Simulated joint distribution of the four regulation quarter totals from drive allocation and period-specific per-drive scoring, summarised as P(quarter q is the unique or shared maximum, weighted 1/N) and P(any quarter total = 0).
nfl.quarter_total_order_statistics.rationale: Highest-scoring-quarter and scoreless-quarter contracts depend on order statistics of four dependent, lumpy totals; marginal quarter totals cannot price them because ties at the top and zero atoms dominate, and Q2/Q4 two-minute effects make the quarters non-exchangeable.

nfl.rating_state_space.label: Team-strength state-space updating rule (preseason prior, process noise, opponent adjustment)
nfl.rating_state_space.measurement: Kalman filter on team offence and defence EPA/play ratings: state_t+1 = 0.6*state_t + 0.4*preseason_prior at season boundary (coefficient estimated by prior-year to next-year correlation 2005+), weekly process variance sigma_p^2 estimated by marginal likelihood, observation = opponent-adjusted game EPA with garbage-time weights; report posterior mean and variance per team as-of previous week.
nfl.rating_state_space.mechanism: Team ratings are latent states updated weekly with an offseason regression to the mean and weekly process noise, with opponent adjustment simultaneously solved.
nfl.rating_state_space.rationale: Different updating speeds produce different mid-season ratings; slow updating misses real changes, fast updating chases noise; the choice is rarely defined in the catalog.

nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error.label: Shared team-rating uncertainty (posterior sd) carried across all games
nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error.measurement: Prior sd = 4.0 points of margin rating at the preseason (assumption: preseason win-total errors have sd about 2.9 wins against a binomial sd of about 2.1, implying a rating sd near 4 points; re-estimate from residuals of own preseason ratings against final ratings over 2002-2025); posterior sd after n games = 1/sqrt(1/prior_sd^2 + n/s^2) where the game-level residual standard deviation is 13.5 points, so s^2 = 13.5^2 = 182.25 points^2. Sample one team-level strength draw per simulation and keep it across all remaining games. Output: sd by team and week.
nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error.mechanism: Posterior standard deviation of each team's latent rating, applied as a common draw across all of that team's games in a simulation.
nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error.rationale: If every game is simulated at a fixed rating, win totals are too concentrated and tail probabilities for 4-win or 13-win teams are underestimated; the shared error is the main reason season win-total distributions are wider than binomial.

nfl.ratings.label: Power ratings and market-implied team strength history
nfl.ratings.measurement: Invert historical spreads/totals/moneylines (games.csv) into team ratings via a Bradley-Terry/ridge fit per season with home edge; also keep Elo-style margin-based rating with MOV cap, QB adjustment (value of starter versus replacement), and 17-game season reversion (~1/3 toward mean). Track the rating at kickoff and the opening-to-close change.
nfl.ratings.mechanism: Closing lines embed injury news, weather and sharp information; the rating implied by spread history is the strongest prior on team quality and encodes information not visible in box scores.
nfl.ratings.rationale: Any model of NFL results must beat or at least calibrate against market-implied strength; the real use is as a prior or control so residual inputs add information instead of re-deriving what the line already contains. Subtle: lines move for QB/injury news, so ratings must be keyed to the lineup the line assumed, not the season average.

nfl.receiving_corps_route_weighted_quali.label: Route-weighted receiving-corps quality for the projected active set
nfl.receiving_corps_route_weighted_quali.measurement: For each receiver, rolling 12-game route-weighted separation, catch rate over expected and YACOE, shrunk toward position mean with k=60 targets; corps score = sum over projected active receivers of projected route share x player score, where route shares are redistributed from the declared inactive list using the last 3 games' conditional shares. Units: standardized yards per attempt over league mean, as-of inactive list time (about 90 minutes pre-kick) or last practice report.
nfl.receiving_corps_route_weighted_quali.mechanism: Aggregate of expected separation, catch-probability-over-expected and yards after catch over expected across the receivers and backs projected to run routes, weighted by projected route share.
nfl.receiving_corps_route_weighted_quali.rationale: The passer's yield depends on who catches the ball. A binary flag for WR1 out ignores that a replacement with a much lower route share and weaker separation changes yards per attempt, and that the effect depends on the whole route tree. Need a number that moves when a name changes on the inactive list.

nfl.red_zone_target_quality.label: Red-zone catcher quality and availability (contested-catch and size-weighted target value)
nfl.red_zone_target_quality.measurement: For each team-week, rz_target_quality = sum over players of (share of team targets inside the opponent 20 over the last 12 games, half-life 6 games) x (player's red-zone catch rate over expected, shrunk to the league mean with k=20 red-zone targets) x (availability weight from the active/inactive status at the as-of time); standardise across teams within season; output the team value and the value lost when the top red-zone target is replaced by the next on the chart. As-of: after the previous game and updated at the inactive list.
nfl.red_zone_target_quality.mechanism: The probability that a red-zone or goal-to-go throw becomes a touchdown depends on who is the target: tall, contested-catch receivers and tight ends convert short throws at higher rates than slot receivers, so QB touchdown counts depend on the supporting cast.
nfl.red_zone_target_quality.rationale: nfl.skill_avail captures absences but not the quality level of red-zone catchers; a QB with a dominant red-zone target has a higher per-attempt TD rate independent of his own skill, and a team's passing-TD count is lost when that player is out or replaced.

nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.label: Rest-of-season statistical projection to the ballot cutoff
nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.measurement: Projected total = banked total + sum over remaining games g of P(plays g) x expected per-game rate_g, where the per-game rate is a 50/50 blend of season-to-date per-game rate and a 3-year prior (shrunk with k=6 games), scaled by opponent defence adjustment from nfl.schedule_strength (+-10 percent cap) and by P(plays g) from nfl.games_played_dist; uncertainty from a negative-binomial per-game sd fitted on 2015-2025. As-of: before the next kickoff window; cutoff = last regular-season game (ballot close date assumed at the end of the regular season, unverified, see u3).
nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.mechanism: Projects each candidate's final regular-season totals by adding expected remaining-game production to banked totals, with a games-played hazard.
nfl.rest_of_season_stat_projection.rationale: Awards are voted on final-season body of work, and Kalshi prices trade in October to January while about half the games remain; ranking by banked stats ignores that a candidate on a bye or with a tough schedule will fall behind. The projection is for production rank, not a price.

nfl.sb_mvp_live_ballot_state.measurement: From live play-by-play, compute every minute: market-free win probability from score differential, time remaining, possession and field position (nflverse-style WP model, no betting lines), and each player's running line; feed to the conditional-credit model with a time-to-ballot-close weight; as-of = play timestamp, never later than the decision time.
nfl.sb_mvp_live_ballot_state.mechanism: During the game the MVP probability is driven by the current leader in visible production on the team that is ahead, evaluated at the time ballots close (fan vote in the fourth quarter).
nfl.sb_mvp_live_ballot_state.rationale: If the markets keep trading into the game, pre-game projections are quickly superseded; the right features are the in-game box score and a market-free win probability from score, time and field position, with a discount for plays after the ballot cut.

nfl.sb_mvp_winner_conditional_credit.label: Winning-team credit allocation (P(MVP | team wins) by player and unit)
nfl.sb_mvp_winner_conditional_credit.measurement: Fit a multinomial or conditional logit on all Super Bowls since 1967 (and playoff winners as extra data) with in-game player covariates: passing yards and TDs, rush and receiving yards, total TDs, defensive TDs and takeaways, game-winning play indicator and position dummy; sacks enter only for 1982+ games (official since 1982) with a missing indicator before, and tackles are excluded as unofficial. Add a QB-premium intercept with a hierarchical prior; predict on simulated box scores from the winner's player projection. Output P(player MVP | team wins) and position aggregates.
nfl.sb_mvp_winner_conditional_credit.mechanism: Model of how credit divides among the winner's players: quarterback line, receivers, running backs, pass rushers, defensive scorers and returners, given the game script that leads to a win.
nfl.sb_mvp_winner_conditional_credit.rationale: Voters pick from the winning team (a single non-winner exception exists), so what matters is which unit posts the visible highlights. A high-passing quarterback line, a defensive touchdown or a decisive turnover can overrule season reputation; the mechanism is a function of in-game box score not season stats, so season-stat awards inputs are weak here.
raw_data: Super Bowl box scores by player

nfl.sb_neutral_site_matchup_win_prob.label: Super Bowl neutral-site matchup win probability (market-free)
nfl.sb_neutral_site_matchup_win_prob.measurement: Combine the own opponent-adjusted team rating with a full-strength lineup adjustment (starter availability at kickoff minus 2 weeks) and zero home-field advantage; both finalists have a two-week gap so no rest term applies to the final itself, while reaching the final uses a bye effect for seeds that skip the wild-card round (rest edge in the divisional round). Convert margin to win probability with a single-game SD of about 13 points; sum over simulated conference-championship pairs. As-of = latest game result and injury vintage; shrink ratings toward the league mean using 10 games of prior weight.
nfl.sb_neutral_site_matchup_win_prob.mechanism: Win probability for each possible pair of conference champions at a neutral site after a two-week break, from full-strength lineups and the playoff overtime rule, then weighted by the chance each pair meets.
nfl.sb_neutral_site_matchup_win_prob.rationale: MVP probability for a player is P(his team reaches the game) times P(wins) times P(he is chosen given a win), so the first two factors are team-level quantities fixed by path and matchup. The full-strength rating, not the season average, applies because injured starters return or are lost in the two weeks and home advantage is absent.

nfl.school_draftable_prospect_pool.label: School draftable-prospect pool (eligible players by school with projected round)

nfl.school_draftable_prospect_pool.mechanism: Count and quality of each school's draft-eligible players (seniors, declared underclassmen, transfers listed under the school the league uses) with per-player probability of being drafted and of going in rounds 1-3.

nfl.score_path_sequence_sim.label: Drive-sequence score-path simulation: largest lead, lead changes and comeback events
nfl.score_path_sequence_sim.measurement: For each game: possessions alternate starting from the coin-toss winner; drive outcome multinomial (TD, FG, turnover, punt, safety, end of half) from team offence vs opposing defence rates (nfl.drive_outcome_by_index style, opponent-adjusted, last 16 games with half-life 8, shrink k=150 drives) modified by score state (lead or trail by 0-8, 9-16, 17+) and time remaining using 2012-2025 state multipliers; points per TD from nfl.scoring_event_point_values; 20,000 simulated games; outputs per game: distribution of max |margin|, number of lead changes (excluding first score), P(eventual winner trailed by >=24), calibrated against 2012-2025 realised frequencies by own-rating expected-margin and expected-total bucket (nfl.own_rating_game_state_prior; no sportsbook spread or total). As-of kickoff.
nfl.score_path_sequence_sim.mechanism: Simulates the alternating drive sequence of both teams with per-drive outcomes and point values, recording the full in-game margin path so path functionals (maximum lead, lead changes, minimum margin of the eventual winner) can be read.
nfl.score_path_sequence_sim.rationale: Final-score models cannot price path contracts: two games with the same final margin can have zero or eight lead changes. The path depends on drive-outcome probabilities by team, on the alternation of possessions, on state-dependent play calling (trailing teams pass and go for it, leaders run clock) and on point values (7, 3, 8, 6, 2), so a simulation that conditions each drive on the current score state is required.

nfl.scoring_event_point_values.label: Scoring package distribution (TD value, extra points, two-point, safety)
nfl.scoring_event_point_values.measurement: Per team: P(XP made | kicker, distance) with k=50 attempts shrinkage; two-point attempt rate by coach and win probability state with k=15; safety rate per game; compute P(TD value in {6,7,8}); as-of start of week.
nfl.scoring_event_point_values.mechanism: Points per TD depend on the extra-point success rate and two-point attempt policy; FG is 3; safeties 2.
nfl.scoring_event_point_values.rationale: Race-to-N lattices depend on the exact increment distribution; treating a TD as 7 misses 6-point and 8-point cases that change which team crosses N first.

nfl.scrimmage_turnover_return_long_tail.label: Long turnover-return tail on scrimmage downs (99+ yard INT, fumble, blocked/missed-FG returns)
nfl.scrimmage_turnover_return_long_tail.measurement: Per team-game, rate of returns >= 99 yards on interceptions, fumbles and missed/blocked FGs from nflverse pbp (return_yards, play_type, interception, fumble_lost, field_goal_result) since 1999; exposure = opponent snaps with yardline_100 <= 10 plus FG attempts of 50+ yards; hierarchical Poisson with team takeaway rate shrunk to league (40 team-games prior); output expected count for remaining games.
nfl.scrimmage_turnover_return_long_tail.mechanism: Interceptions and fumbles in the defence's own red zone, and missed or blocked field goals fielded in the end zone, can be returned 99-109 yards on a play that began as a scrimmage down.
nfl.scrimmage_turnover_return_long_tail.rationale: If Kalshi counts these as plays from scrimmage, they are a more frequent route to 99+ yards than offensive gains from the own 1 and the own-1 exposure is no longer a bound. Exposure is opponent red-zone and goal-line pass attempts and long FG attempts, not own-1 snaps.

nfl.season_extreme_era_base_rate.label: Era-adjusted historical distribution of season maxima (margin, total, rushing yards)
nfl.season_extreme_era_base_rate.measurement: For 1978-2025 seasons compute max margin, max total and max single-game rushing yards; scale for games per season (16 to 17) and league scoring per game relative to the season mean; fit GEV per statistic with a scoring-environment covariate; report P(season max > rung) for the 2026 environment with bootstrap intervals. Report per-rung empirical frequency (seasons with exceedance / seasons) beside the GEV estimate; for the 225 rung use count of 225+ games per season, not a record-break model.
nfl.season_extreme_era_base_rate.mechanism: Per-season maxima of game margin, game total and single-game rushing yards over past regular seasons, adjusted for the scoring environment and number of games.
nfl.season_extreme_era_base_rate.rationale: Rungs differ in rarity: the 109.5 total lies beyond the post-merger record (about 106), the 51.5 margin has been exceeded at least five times since the merger (59, 54, 59, 55 and 58 points in 1976, 1989, 2009, 2011 and 2012), roughly once a decade, and 225+ rushing yards recurs across seasons. Base rates are therefore set separately per rung: seasons with any margin above 45, any total above 90 and any 200-yard rusher calibrate per-game tail fits and guard against overconfident extrapolation.

nfl.season_participation_streak_hazard.label: Weekly miss hazard compounded over a season (every-week participation)
nfl.season_participation_streak_hazard.measurement: Discrete-time logistic hazard of missing week w given active-roster membership, trained on 2012-2025 player-weeks: covariates = position, age, prior-season games missed, current injury designation, snaps per game (exposure), week >= 17 x team clinched flag; include a frailty term (player random effect, shrinkage from 3 prior seasons); P(streak) = prod_w (1 - h_w) over remaining scheduled games via simulation that carries injury state forward; as-of market time.
nfl.season_participation_streak_hazard.mechanism: Probability that a player takes a snap in every team game of a season, from a weekly hazard of missing a game through injury, rest or benching.
nfl.season_participation_streak_hazard.rationale: Every-week participation is a long product of weekly survivals; a weekly miss rate that looks small compounds to large season-level failure probability, and missed games cluster after injuries, so independence understates the streak's survival among durable players and overstates it for injury-prone ones.

nfl.single_game_ceiling_tail_model.label: Single-game ceiling tail model for any-game highs
nfl.single_game_ceiling_tail_model.measurement: For each player estimate per-game score distribution with a Poisson-touchdown plus compound yardage model (components from stage s2-s4) and a Pareto tail above the 90th percentile fitted on position-level game scores from 2012-2025; P(max over N remaining games >= x) = 1 - prod(1 - p_g(x)) with p_g adjusted for game-specific total and availability; add an upward correlation correction via nfl.fantasy_component_and_stack_covariance. Output P at several thresholds by remaining games.
nfl.single_game_ceiling_tail_model.mechanism: Probability that a player's single-game score exceeds a high threshold (34, 49 points) in a given game, based on per-game distributions with an extreme-value tail.
nfl.single_game_ceiling_tail_model.rationale: Season-high contracts depend on rare big games rather than the mean; the maximum of 17 games grows with the log of games and is dominated by touchdown clusters and long plays.
raw_data: player-game fantasy points history by position

nfl.slate_max_tie_mass.label: Probability and size of ties at the weekly maximum
nfl.slate_max_tie_mass.measurement: Empirical 2002-2025: share of weeks with a tied maximum team score and tied maximum game total, by number of teams playing; model: simulate integer team-score PMFs per team-game (from nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean, the catalog key-number PMF input), compute P(tie at max) and expected payout floor(100/N)/100 per named team; calibrate simulated tie rates to the empirical share. As-of week start.
nfl.slate_max_tie_mass.mechanism: Probability that two or more games (or teams) share the highest total (or team score) in a week, and the expected payout under the $1/N rounded-down rule.
nfl.slate_max_tie_mass.rationale: Team scores cluster on key values (17, 20, 24, 27, 31, 34) so ties at the top among 26-32 teams are common enough to change expected value; game-total ties at the maximum are rarer but not negligible. The dead-heat rule makes a tied favourite worth well below 1.

nfl.slate_running_extreme_state.label: Running season extreme to date and remaining eligible games
nfl.slate_running_extreme_state.measurement: After each completed game: max |margin|, max total (with OT), max single-game rushing yards by any player; boolean cleared per rung; remaining games list with week index and model mismatch per game. P(YES) = 1 if cleared else 1 - prod_g (1 - p_g) with p_g from the tail inputs and a shared-error correction. As-of final official score of the last completed game.
nfl.slate_running_extreme_state.mechanism: For season-maximum contracts, the realised largest margin, total and single-game rushing yards so far, whether the rung is already cleared, and the list of remaining regular-season games define the live state.
nfl.slate_running_extreme_state.rationale: A season threshold is a first-passage event: once cleared it is YES, otherwise probability decays with each completed game. The relevant remaining exposure is not uniform: late-season weeks with rested starters and eliminated teams carry more blowout potential than mid-season weeks.

nfl.slate_total_extremes.label: Slate-level highest-total and largest-margin order statistics
nfl.slate_total_extremes.measurement: For each slate game g draw total from the game-total distribution (mean from nfl.pace/off_epa model, SD from nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd analog for totals), include shared weather correlation (rho from nfl.corr), simulate 20,000 slates; report P(game g has highest total) and expected payout under $1/N split; as-of kickoff vintages for each game.
nfl.slate_total_extremes.mechanism: Joint distribution of the week's game totals and margins, for maxima and tie-splitting.
nfl.slate_total_extremes.rationale: The highest-scoring game market and weekly max margin are maxima over 13-16 games with heterogeneous means; ties split the payout so exact integer ties matter.
raw_data: game total distributions, slate composition (bye weeks), weather

nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definition.label: Sleeper scoring settings, group membership and correction timing
nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definition.measurement: Archive Sleeper's scoring settings (points per yard, per touchdown, per reception, kicker table) and each week's published points at game end, at 24 hours and at settlement; flag differences from the standard stat sheet; keep a table of Sleeper position assignment as of the expiration date; compute a score from official stats and compare with the Sleeper value (error in points).
nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definition.mechanism: Mapping from official stats to Sleeper's default full-PPR points, including kicker and bonus rules, the position group each player is assigned to and when Sleeper publishes or corrects totals.
nfl.sleeper_scoring_and_group_definition.rationale: The contract settles on Sleeper's number, not on the league's stat; a player's position group (WR/RB/TE/QB), rookie flag, rounding and timing of the published value determine the outcome and cannot be assumed from another fantasy platform.
raw_data: Sleeper player metadata (fantasy_positions), weekly stats, scoring settings

nfl.snap_appearance_given_active.label: P(at least one snap | active) by role
nfl.snap_appearance_given_active.measurement: From snap counts 2016-2025: fraction of active player-games with at least one offensive, defensive or special-teams snap by position and depth slot; shrinkage k=10 games; adjust for spread (blowouts raise backup snaps); output separate probabilities with and without special-teams snaps.
nfl.snap_appearance_given_active.mechanism: Probability that an active player plays at least one snap (including or excluding special teams) by depth slot and script.
nfl.snap_appearance_given_active.rationale: The contract requires a snap, so an active emergency QB or deep rotation player may resolve NO; the base rate varies by role.
raw_data: snap counts per player-game by unit (off, def, ST)

nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.label: Win-streak and undefeated-hazard path model across 32 teams
nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.measurement: Do not build a separate simulator: use the single shared season simulator nfl.standings_sim (with the shared rating-uncertainty draw and tie probability of the win-totals record, 0.25 percent per game and rating prior sd of 4.0 points as the shared assumptions) run on REMAINING games only, conditioned on the results already played as of the current week (completed scores, ties, each team's current win streak and undefeated flag, banked 60+ yard field goals and tie count), current injuries and quarterback status. For each of 100,000 runs record: the longest streak (under both tie treatments, see u2) for each team, the week of each team's first loss (ties not losses; same-week first losses tied), season tie count and 60-yard field goal count (banked + simulated), and the worst-to-first indicator; output probabilities for each contract rung.
nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.mechanism: Probability distribution of the longest win streak, the week of the last first loss, and the number of ties, from a correlated season simulation with shared rating uncertainty.
nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path.rationale: Streak and undefeated contracts depend on the sequence of game outcomes and on strength dispersion, not just on win totals; ties break streaks without being losses, and a bye week is an unrecorded week. It is now week 9 of the season, so most of these contracts are partly decided by banked results and the input must carry the current season state, not restart at Week 1.
raw_data: schedule order, byes, last-season division ranks, completed results to date, current streak and undefeated flags

nfl.supplemental_draft_mechanics.label: Supplemental Draft mechanics (eligibility petition, tiered lottery order, bid cost)
nfl.supplemental_draft_mechanics.measurement: Count Supplemental Draft years with and without picks over 1977-2026 for a base rate; model P(selected) per eligible player from projected round (a bid costs the same-round pick next year, so teams bid only if the player is worth it), team round-pick inventory, and the league ruling date; as-of = league announcement of eligibility and the date of the draft.
nfl.supplemental_draft_mechanics.mechanism: Supplemental Draft eligibility via petition, an order set by a lottery within record-based tiers (non-playoff teams grouped by wins, then playoff teams), and the bid rule that costs a team its same-round pick in the next regular draft.
nfl.supplemental_draft_mechanics.rationale: This draft is held rarely and picks only the few players the league declares eligible; whether a named player is selected depends on whether any team will pay a future pick, so the key variables are eligibility ruling, the player's expected round and team needs, not consensus board ranking.

nfl.td_play_length_by_source.label: Touchdown play length by source (scrimmage, interception, fumble, kick and punt return, missed-FG return)
nfl.td_play_length_by_source.measurement: Tabulate touchdown length by scoring route from play-by-play for 1999-2026 (yards_gained for scrimmage; return_yards for returns; kick-return TDs measured from the catch spot), with counts per season, the per-season maximum and minimum, and per-route rate per 1,000 snaps with the same tail model as above; record both with and without return TDs so that either contract reading can be priced.
nfl.td_play_length_by_source.mechanism: Distribution of touchdown lengths split by scoring route, because returns can exceed 99 yards and short touchdowns come from goal-line runs and sneaks.
nfl.td_play_length_by_source.rationale: The single-game TD-length buckets read official play-by-play distances and do not exclude returns, so the route mix matters: return TDs reach 100-109 yards, while fumbles recovered in the end zone give 0-yard TDs that can set the minimum. Season-wide the minimum is almost always 0-1 yards, but per game it depends on how many TDs are scored and how.

nfl.team_first_td_attribution.label: Team first-TD scorer attribution history
nfl.team_first_td_attribution.measurement: For each team-game, record the scorer of the team's first TD and the yard line; compute recency-weighted shares (half-life 20 team games, includes prior-season games at 0.5 weight) and shrink to the player's full-game xTD share with k=10 team first-TD events; output: scorer share and expected yardline.
nfl.team_first_td_attribution.mechanism: The scorer of a team's first TD is drawn from a distribution that differs from the full-game distribution because the first score arises in scripted and early-down contexts.
nfl.team_first_td_attribution.rationale: Scorer shares in first TDs are rated off about 17 events per team-season, so they need strong shrinkage to the full-game xTD share; naive 'first TD hit rate' is nearly pure noise.
raw_data: pbp: game_id, posteam, touchdown, td_player_id, yardline_100, drive number

nfl.team_points_for_against_rates.label: Separate offence and defence scoring rates for season and weekly extremes
nfl.team_points_for_against_rates.measurement: For each team compute opponent-adjusted points per game for offence and defence separately: ridge regression of team points on offence and opposing-defence indicators with home indicator, over the last 17 games weighted exp(-ln2 x games_ago/8) with a one-third reversion to league mean before the season (offence k=6 games, defence k=6 games shrink to mean). Simulate remaining games conditioned on points already banked (as of the current week): team season points = banked + sum of simulated scores, each score drawn from a negative binomial with mean from the team's own rates (sd about 9.5 points per team-game, an assumption to refit) and a shared per-team rate draw (sd 1.2 points per game). Weekly high score = max over that week's 32 (or fewer on byes) simulated scores. Output P(team has min/max points scored/allowed) with 1/N ties, and P(team has the weekly high). As-of: after the last completed game.
nfl.team_points_for_against_rates.mechanism: Estimates each team's points scored and points allowed per game as separate rates with their own uncertainty, so that season scoring extremes and the weekly highest-scoring team can be simulated.
nfl.team_points_for_against_rates.rationale: A single margin rating cannot give points for and points against; the most/least points scored and allowed are extremes over 32 teams that depend on pace, defence and offence separately, and the weekly high score is the maximum of 32 correlated-through-nothing but heavy-tailed team scores. Contracts are priced from the right tail of each team's score distribution.
raw_data: schedules: game_id, week, team scores, home flag
pbp: plays and epa per team

nfl.team_positional_need_and_qb_regime.label: Team positional need and quarterback regime (who needs what at their slot)
nfl.team_positional_need_and_qb_regime.measurement: Score need per team-position as a weighted sum of (starter age above position median, contract years remaining below 2, last-season EPA or PFF-style grade percentile, depth chart gap after free agency); QB regime coded from contract guarantees, recent draft capital and benching history. Refresh weekly until the draft; as-of = last transaction timestamp; shrink by position-group priors with 10 team-years constant.

nfl.team_positional_need_and_qb_regime.rationale: Slot buyers choose among a handful of boards; need breaks ties between near-equal prospects and sets quarterback pressure: a top-3 holder without a franchise QB faces a qualitatively different incentive than a holder with a long-term deal. Free agency and trades before the draft shift need so a stale vintage is wrong.
raw_data: roster and depth chart by position

nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean.label: Own-mean team score probability mass function with key-number structure (market-free)
nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean.measurement: From all regular-season team-games 2010-2025 take the integer final score; bin by the model's own pre-game expected team points (from nfl.drive_result_lattice means; no sportsbook line) in 1-point bins from 10 to 35; fit within each bin a discrete mixture: negative-binomial body (dispersion estimated per bin, roughly sd 9-10 points) plus a kernel-smoothed empirical correction ratio at scores 0,3,6,7,9,10,13,14,16,17,20,21,23,24,27,28 (correction = observed/NB frequency, shrunk to 1 with k=60 team-games per score). Include overtime points in the pmf and also keep a regulation-only pmf, selecting by contract (KXNFLBOTH counts overtime; KXNFLTEAMTOTAL unstated, see u1). Output: P(score >= n) for n in 0..60, as-of the final pre-kickoff mean.
nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean.mechanism: Converts the model's own expected points for a team into a discrete integer score distribution that carries the extra mass at 3, 6, 7, 10 and 14, so every rung of the ladder is read from one pmf.
nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean.rationale: The catalog score residual is defined around the closing spread and total, and the team-total split is derived from the same lines, so both are market echoes. The key-number lumpiness is real, but it must be fitted around own predicted means; otherwise the model inherits the market's mean and the comparison with Kalshi prices is circular.
raw_data: schedules: game_id, team scores, overtime flag

nfl.team_season_stat_accrual.label: Team season-statistic accrual for non-points team totals (net passing, rushing yards) and late-season rest scaling
nfl.team_season_stat_accrual.measurement: Points for/against: use the season-total simulation of nfl.team_points_for_against_rates unchanged (its banked-plus-remaining draws and 1/N extreme rule), only multiplying Weeks 17-18 expected scores by the starter-rest factor from nfl.clinched_rest_starter_probability. Net passing yards per remaining game g = expected team dropbacks (nfl.pace x nfl.proe) x [(1 - sack rate) x gross yards per attempt - sack rate x mean sack yards (about 6.5)], with sack rate = team sack rate allowed x opponent pressure factor, gross yards per attempt opponent-adjusted over the last 17 games (half-life 8 games, shrink to league mean with k=6 games); rushing yards analogously from rush attempts x opponent-adjusted yards per carry. Per-game sd from 2012-2025 residuals (about 70 net passing yards); team strength errors are the same per-simulation draw used by the points model (nfl.rating_uncertainty_shared_error), not an extra one. Sum over remaining games plus banked total; 20,000 simulations. As-of the latest completed game.
nfl.team_season_stat_accrual.mechanism: Projects a team's final regular-season net passing or rushing yards as banked total plus a simulated sum over its remaining games, and applies Weeks 17-18 starter-rest scaling to every team-season total; season points for/against are taken from nfl.team_points_for_against_rates, not recomputed.
nfl.team_season_stat_accrual.rationale: Team extremes and team specials settle on season totals, so a per-game rating is not enough: byes, the remaining opponents' defences or offences, late-season starter rest and the sack deduction in net passing yards change the remaining sum. The extreme over teams then needs every team's total jointly simulated with shared rating uncertainty.

nfl.team_stat_accounting_constraints.label: Team-to-player accounting constraints for same-game legs
nfl.team_stat_accounting_constraints.measurement: Compute, from historical player-games, the distribution of the share of team yards and TDs captured by the top-k players; define a Dirichlet-multinomial allocation for each team-game with concentration from the prior 17 games (shrink k=20); enforce sum(player) = team and floor for unlisted players. Output joint distribution over pairs of player legs on one team; as-of previous game.
nfl.team_stat_accounting_constraints.mechanism: Individual player outputs must sum to team outputs, so player legs on one team compete for a fixed pool, and incompatible leg sets have zero joint probability.
nfl.team_stat_accounting_constraints.rationale: Gaussian correlations allow two teammates to both hit first-TD legs or both clear very large yardage lines; the identity-based approach prevents impossible combinations and captures negative dependence among teammates.
raw_data: pbp: player ids by yards, TD and target
