nfl.team_total_split.label: Team-points share model (implied total and spread to team means)
nfl.team_total_split.measurement: Compute implied team means from the closing spread and total (mu_A = (T - s)/2 etc.), adjust for team-specific scoring variance and key-number structure; compare team total quotes to the implied pair to detect inconsistent pricing.
nfl.team_total_split.mechanism: The game total and spread jointly imply each team's expected points: team A = (total + spread-to-A)/2; team totals markets depend on this split and on variance of each team separately.
nfl.team_total_split.rationale: Team total and combined markets must be consistent with the game market; the split depends on spread and total only if the market is efficient; deviations signal mispricing; allowing for scoring styles (high-variance team) matters.

nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.label: Teammate and look-alike candidate vote-splitting penalty
nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.measurement: From historical AP voting records (last 20 seasons), estimate a Plackett-Luce or Dirichlet model where each candidate's latent score includes a penalty beta x (score of the best same-team or same-position rival); estimate beta by maximum likelihood with candidates having at least one vote; shrink beta toward 0 with a ridge prior (lambda tuned by leave-one-season-out). Output: winner probabilities after the split correction.
nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.mechanism: Reduction in a candidate's vote share caused by another strong candidate with the same team, position or narrative.
nfl.teammate_vote_split_penalty.rationale: Plurality voting splits similar support: two quarterbacks on the same team or two edge rushers with similar sack counts take votes from each other, so independent win probabilities overstate the sum and understate a third candidate's chance.
raw_data: AP vote shares by candidate-season, team, position

nfl.total_distribution_tail.label: Both-tail model of game total points
nfl.total_distribution_tail.measurement: Fit a skewed distribution (shifted lognormal or discrete mixture of negative-binomial team scores) to 2000+ game totals conditioned on the model expected total (sum of the market-free team means from nfl.model_team_points_mean, not a betting total) in terciles and weather regime; add empirical atoms at key totals (37, 41, 43, 44, 47, 51) as residuals of a smoothed fit with Dirichlet smoothing; estimate P(total >= 70), P(<=24) with bootstrap CI (about 5,000 games); validate calibration by decile of model expected total; as-of start of season and each week.
nfl.total_distribution_tail.mechanism: Tail probabilities of the combined score beyond about 1.8 SD in each direction conditional on expected total and environment.
nfl.total_distribution_tail.rationale: TOTALPRECISE ladders extend to 98.5 and TOTAL to 24.5; these rungs are priced on tails, which a normal approximation gets wrong because totals are right-skewed with heavy upper tail from blowout cascades and short-field TDs. The expected total it conditions on is the market-free model total, so the tail does not inherit the line.
raw_data: final scores since 2000, wind, roof, model expected-total regime (market-free)

nfl.total_plays_state_model.label: State-conditional total plays model (mutual tempo with lead effects)
nfl.total_plays_state_model.measurement: Regress total plays per game on each team's neutral seconds per play, PROE, own and opponent run rate, expected absolute margin (from model, not market), pass-completion rate and penalty rate, with team and opponent random effects; use 2015+ games; shrink coefficients; output expected plays and SD; as-of previous week.
nfl.total_plays_state_model.mechanism: Total plays are a function of both teams' seconds per play, run rates, expected lead state and clock stoppages rather than the average of two neutral paces.
nfl.total_plays_state_model.rationale: Neutral pace is measured when the score is close; actual plays depend on how the game goes, and a favourite protecting a lead cuts plays substantially; the combination of two paces is not additive.
raw_data: pbp: game_id, plays by team, seconds per play, qtr, score_differential, penalty

nfl.trick_play_and_goal_line_pass_events.label: Rare play-call events: non-QB pass attempts and pass attempts from the 1-yard line
nfl.trick_play_and_goal_line_pass_events.measurement: Non-QB pass: count of pass attempts by players whose roster position is not QB per team-game over the last 3 seasons, shrunk to league rate (about 0.15 per game, to recompute) with k=40 team-games, coach random effect; P(any in game) = 1 - exp(-(rate_A + rate_B)). Pass from the 1: expected snaps with yardline_100 <= 1 per team-game (from drives reaching the 1, last 2 seasons, shrink k=30) x team pass share on those snaps (shrink to league about 0.35 with k=25 snaps) counting only pass_attempt == 1 (sacks and scrambles excluded); P(at least one) by Poisson. As-of kickoff with the active roster.
nfl.trick_play_and_goal_line_pass_events.mechanism: Per-team rates of non-quarterback pass attempts (trick plays, fake punts) and of pass calls on snaps from on or inside the opponent's 1, combined with the expected number of snaps from the 1.
nfl.trick_play_and_goal_line_pass_events.rationale: Both contracts are low-rate Bernoulli events whose base rate differs strongly by coach and personnel (a former-quarterback receiver, a Tush-Push team that never passes from the 1); league averages mislead, but team samples are tiny, so heavy shrinkage toward the league rate is essential and stakes may raise trick-play frequency.
raw_data: pbp: game_id, posteam, passer_player_id, pass_attempt, sack, qb_scramble, yardline_100, down

free_sources: Pro Football Reference awards and voting (free_scrape)
nfl.vote_outcome_model.label: Vote-share model for awards and the Top 100 list
nfl.vote_outcome_model.measurement: Multinomial logit of historical winner on candidate features (team win%, individual statistical rank, prior award wins, position, narrative flags) for each award 2000-2025 with k=3 pseudo-observations shrinkage; for T100, ordered logit on previous rank, change in production, position group and age; compute P(candidate=winner) and P(rank=#r); as-of announcement date. Aggregation layer: for division or conference specials (KXNFLMVPSPECIALS, KXNFLOPOYSPECIALS, DPOY specials) P(group) = sum over candidates of P(win) by the team of record at announcement time, with the sampled 1/N co-winner payout rule; for Executive of the Year the 'Tie/Co-Winners' strike gets P(tie) = historical co-winner frequency in the award's own history (to be counted from its published list) shrunk toward the pooled frequency across comparable awards with k=10 awards.
nfl.vote_outcome_model.mechanism: Winner or rank probability from candidate quality, narrative, previous votes, timing and electorate composition.
nfl.vote_outcome_model.rationale: Awards and ranks are decided by a small electorate with identifiable biases (position, team success, prior awards); the leader's share is concentrated.
raw_data: historical winners and vote tallies, candidate stats, previous T100 ranks

nfl.voter_exposure_and_straw_poll_signal.label: Voter exposure: primetime games, national attention and public straw polls
nfl.voter_exposure_and_straw_poll_signal.measurement: Primetime-game counts and share of the candidate's yards or touchdowns in those games to date; rank in published straw polls (e.g. by members of the voting panel) at each week (rank points via Borda). Combined into one score with weights from historical regression on vote share, as-of each Tuesday; no betting prices or Kalshi quotes used.
nfl.voter_exposure_and_straw_poll_signal.mechanism: Count of primetime and national games for the candidate's team so far and standing in published writers' ballots or straw polls from non-market sources.
nfl.voter_exposure_and_straw_poll_signal.rationale: Voters see the nationally televised games and discuss candidates in public straw polls; this is a signal of voter sentiment distinct from production and is not a market price.

nfl.weather_delay_hazard.label: Game weather-delay hazard (lightning and severe weather)
nfl.weather_delay_hazard.measurement: Logistic model on 2010-2025 games (outcome: any weather delay from game books/news): features = roof (open/retractable/dome), month, kickoff local hour, regional climatological thunderstorm-day frequency for the month (NOAA), and at forecast time the NWS thunderstorm probability for the kickoff window +/- 3 hours; shrink venue effects toward roof-type means with k=40 games; as-of the 24h and 3h forecast vintages.
nfl.weather_delay_hazard.mechanism: Probability of any official weather delay (pre-start or in-game) for a scheduled game, from roof type, location climatology, month, kickoff hour and the thunderstorm forecast.
nfl.weather_delay_hazard.rationale: Weather delays are almost always lightning within the stadium's radius at open-air venues in early-season afternoon or evening games; fixed domes are near zero and retractable roofs depend on roof policy, so a generic weather input does not capture the event.
raw_data: schedules: game_id, stadium, roof, kickoff time
NWS thunderstorm probability forecasts by location and hour

free_sources: nflverse schedules (wind, temp as measured at game)
nfl.weather_total_response.label: Weather dose-response function for totals (wind, cold, precipitation, roof)
nfl.weather_total_response.measurement: Hierarchical regression of total points residual (game total minus team-baseline expectation from EPA model) on wind (piecewise linear with knots 10, 15, 20 mph), temperature (knots 32, 50), precipitation flag, dome flag; 2010+ games; shrink with k=100 games per bin; use forecast vintages 24 and 3 hours pregame and propagate forecast error as measurement noise; as-of pregame forecast.
nfl.weather_total_response.mechanism: Estimated effect on expected total points of wind speed, temperature and precipitation categories with roof interactions.
nfl.weather_total_response.rationale: Weather effects are strongly nonlinear: below 10 mph wind is negligible, above 15-20 mph reduces totals by several points; forecast error needs to be handled at the pregame time. Historical fits use observed (not forecast) conditions until a season of forecast capture exists.
raw_data: game-time observed wind/temp, forecast vintages, roof

nfl.week_running_state_by_window.label: Within-week realised scores by kickoff window and market close time
nfl.week_running_state_by_window.measurement: At each timestamp t in the week: running max game total M_g(t) and running max team score M_t(t) over completed games (final scores, OT included), the list of games not yet started with kickoff times, and for each remaining game P(total > M_g(t)) and P(team score >= M_t(t)) from the integer score PMFs (nfl.team_score_pmf_own_mean), with ties at the bar counted as dead heats. The named game or team's probability is the conditional argmax probability given the running bar. As-of the last completed final score; capture the market close timestamp so that positions are only evaluated before it. Units points and games.
nfl.week_running_state_by_window.mechanism: For the weekly argmax contracts, the highest game total and highest team score already realised after the Thursday, international, early Sunday and late Sunday windows condition what the remaining games must exceed, and the market close time relative to each window decides how much of that is already known.
nfl.week_running_state_by_window.rationale: Unlike season thresholds, a weekly argmax is partly settled before the last kickoff: after the early window a 55-point game or a 45-point team score sets a running bar that the late games and Monday night rarely beat, so the named game's or team's probability collapses or rises discretely as windows finish. Ignoring the running maximum treats a live market as if it were pre-week.
raw_data: schedules.game_id, week, gameday, gametime, home_score, away_score

nfl.weekly_field_projection_grid.label: Weekly full-pool projection grid and correlation by game
nfl.weekly_field_projection_grid.measurement: For each week and position pool (WR, RB, TE, QB) project every player with at least 5 percent of position snap share: mean and variance from the component model, game environment effect from the own-model projected team points (nfl.off_epa, nfl.def_epa and nfl.pace; never a sportsbook total) shared across the game's players, and a probability of inactivity from the injury vintage; simulate 20,000 weeks to compute P(rank = 1) and P(rank <= 5) for each player including ties at the cutoff (1/N).
nfl.weekly_field_projection_grid.mechanism: Projected distribution of fantasy points for every player in a position pool in the week, including bye weeks, inactives and game environment, with shared game effects.
nfl.weekly_field_projection_grid.rationale: Weekly leader and top-5 contracts are decided across the whole pool, so the probability for a listed player depends on how many other strong options play that week, and on shootouts that lift several players together.

nfl.weekly_leader_threshold_distribution.label: Distribution of the weekly leader's value by position and statistic
nfl.weekly_leader_threshold_distribution.measurement: For each position and statistic, from 2010-2025 weeks collect the weekly maximum and top-5 values; fit a generalized extreme value distribution by position; condition on number of games in the week (Thursday, Monday, bye-heavy weeks) and weather. Output P(player i is the weekly max) via simulation of the active-player field with player-specific distributions.
nfl.weekly_leader_threshold_distribution.mechanism: Baseline distribution of the single-game maximum over all players of a position in a given week and the number of near-miss contenders.
nfl.weekly_leader_threshold_distribution.rationale: The weekly leader market is decided by the top of a very large field; the winner's threshold, not the favourite's mean, sets the chance, and the leader's value is heavy-tailed.
raw_data: player-week stats, number of games in the week

nfl.weekly_qb_depth_slot_model.label: Weekly QB depth-chart slot probabilities (QB1, QB2) per team
nfl.weekly_qb_depth_slot_model.measurement: For each team-week, start from the previous chart order; apply P(QB1 changes) from nfl.qb_change_hazard and injury status; conditional on a change, assign the new QB1 by challenger rank (nfl.qb_challenger_prior); QB2 = highest-ranked remaining QB with rank score from draft capital, preseason snaps with the first and second team, contract APY and coach statements (logit fit on 2016-2025 chart snapshots); injured-but-listed retained per team policy (team fixed effect for keeping injured QBs listed, shrunk k=20 weeks); as-of the latest published chart before close.
nfl.weekly_qb_depth_slot_model.mechanism: Probability that each of a team's quarterbacks is listed QB1 or QB2 on the week's official depth chart, propagating QB1 changes down the chart.
nfl.weekly_qb_depth_slot_model.rationale: Starter and backup designation markets are coupled: a QB1 change promotes the QB2 and opens the QB2 slot, and teams differ in chart policy (co-starters, injured players kept listed), so a slot-level model is needed rather than a starter hazard alone.
raw_data: depth chart snapshots: team, week, position, depth order, player_id, publication date
QB draft slot and contract APY

nfl.weekly_slate_composition.label: Weekly slate size, byes and game windows
nfl.weekly_slate_composition.measurement: From the official schedule as of the week's first kickoff: list of games, teams on bye, kickoff windows, roof status; N_games, N_teams; flag postponed or relocated games and their week assignment. Recompute after any schedule change; units counts.
nfl.weekly_slate_composition.mechanism: Which teams and games are in the week's slate: byes remove teams, Week 18 includes all 32, and international or Thursday games are part of the same week, setting N for the argmax.
nfl.weekly_slate_composition.rationale: With no information the argmax share is about 1/N, and N ranges from about 13 to 16 games and 26 to 32 teams; bye-heavy weeks lift every remaining team's share. A team on bye has zero probability, which the market text does not say explicitly.
raw_data: schedules.game_id, week, gameday, home_team, away_team, roof

nfl.with_without_target_redistribution.label: With/without target redistribution matrix for the projected inactive set
nfl.with_without_target_redistribution.measurement: For each team-season from 2018, compute each receiver's target share and TPRR in games without teammate X versus with X (X = a top-3 target earner), requiring at least 4 games without X over the last 3 seasons, else use a position-role template pooled across teams (shrink with k=40 targets). Apply to the projected inactive list at the last available timestamp. Output: expected target share vector summing to 1 and a standard error per receiver.
nfl.with_without_target_redistribution.mechanism: Conditional split of routes, targets and air yards among remaining receivers when a given teammate does not play.
nfl.with_without_target_redistribution.rationale: The generic target-competition input says teammates matter; what a model needs is the share each remaining player gains when a specific player is out, because slot, outside and tight end absorbers behave differently and the gain is not proportional to current share.
raw_data: pbp: receiver_id, target flag, air_yards, game_id

free_sources: NFL.com Walter Payton Man of the Year nominee announcements (manual)
nfl.wpmoty_nominee_profile.label: Walter Payton Man of the Year nominee profile: community record, prior nominations and visibility
nfl.wpmoty_nominee_profile.measurement: For each nominee-year 2010-2025: number of prior nominations, years in the league, Pro Bowl count (standing proxy), foundation existence and age in years, count of national news articles on the charity in the 12 months before announcement (manual or news-API count). Multinomial logit over the year's 32 nominees fitted to past winners with ridge penalty; shrink coefficients toward equal probability with k=8 award-years. As-of nominee announcement (December).
nfl.wpmoty_nominee_profile.mechanism: Ranks the 32 team nominees by indicators the selection panel uses: scale and tenure of the nominee's charitable work, prior nominations, veteran status and media visibility of the cause.
nfl.wpmoty_nominee_profile.rationale: The award ignores on-field statistics beyond standing; repeat nominees, long-running foundations and veterans near retirement win disproportionately. There is no structured data on charitable work, so the input is a hand-coded profile with a strong prior on repeat nominees.
raw_data: nominee list by year and team
prior nominations, seasons played, Pro Bowls
foundation founding year and news counts

nfl.zero_snap_active_risk.label: Active-but-zero-snap and protected-void probability
nfl.zero_snap_active_risk.measurement: P(no snap | active) = fraction of last 12 active games with zero offensive snaps, shrunk with a beta prior by depth-chart slot (k=6); P(first-half-only) = fraction of active games with snaps in 1H and none in 2H, plus a Friday-designation uplift from past data; as-of 90-minute inactive list.
nfl.zero_snap_active_risk.mechanism: A player can be active and take no snap (RB3, TE3, gadget WR), which voids the contract, and protected contracts void on first-half-only exposure.
nfl.zero_snap_active_risk.rationale: The contract is conditional on a snap; ignoring this overstates a low-usage player's effective price and misses the void probability that determines how much capital is truly at risk.
